Steel-thread proof — a clicked file and a clicked td issue in a live Sidecar
docs/plans/active/preview-pane-tree-and-doc-panes.md, and the click-placement
default in internal/plugins/workspace/pane_placement.go

The journey this work exists for, driven end to end in a real Sidecar process:
a shell filling the preview, a file link clicked into a vertical split, a td id
clicked into a horizontal split below that file — terminal in the left column at
full height, document above issue in the right one. Then the same layout after a
real quit and reopen, and a second td click landing in the issue leaf that is
already open rather than growing the tree.

Unlike the M0 proof, this one does reach the multi-leaf composition: the harness
can inject SGR mouse reports on the host pane's stdin, so the clicks below are
the user's clicks, parsed by the running binary's own mouse handling.

Method
------
One binary, built at the head of this slice, driven on private tmux servers and
a private state tree. Captures are the host pane's ANSI-stripped text with
trailing spaces removed; the clicks are SGR mouse presses and releases sent with
`tmux-drive.sh type`, at coordinates read out of the preceding capture — so each
click lands on a cell the binary actually drew a link into.

`td` is a five-line stub on the launched process's PATH answering
`td show <id> -f json` from the id alone. The issue bodies below are therefore
deterministic, and no real td database was read. Sidecar was launched through a
wrapper that prepends the stub's directory to PATH, because the drive harness
sets the launched command and not its environment.

Isolation (`./scripts/tmux-drive.sh paths` before the run)
  launch repo   /private/tmp/sidecar-steel-fixture  (a git repo holding clicked.md)
  run dir       /private/tmp/sidecar-steel-501
  outer server  -L sidecar-drive under that run dir's TMUX_TMPDIR
  inner tmux    /private/tmp/sidecar-steel-501/tmux/tmux-501/default
  state home    /private/tmp/sidecar-steel-501/state
  config        /private/tmp/sidecar-steel-501/config/config.json
  SIDECAR_ISOLATED_STATE=1
The machine's default tmux server was never started, stopped, or sent a command.

Reproduce
---------
  go build -o /tmp/sidecar-steel-bin/sidecar-real ./cmd/sidecar
  # stub td and a PATH wrapper in /tmp/sidecar-steel-bin, then, with
  # SIDECAR_DRIVE_RUN_DIR=/tmp/sidecar-steel-501,
  # SIDECAR_DRIVE_REPO=/tmp/sidecar-steel-fixture and
  # SIDECAR_BIN=/tmp/sidecar-steel-bin/sidecar-wrapped:
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh start 200 50
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh keys 4                       # workspaces
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh keys C-n                     # a shell to click in
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh inner-type %0 'printf "wrote clicked.md:1\nfollow-up is td-1a2b3c\n"'
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh inner-keys %0 Enter          -> 01-terminal-full-width
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh type $'\e[<0;92;6M'; ... $'\e[<0;92;6m'   -> 02-after-file-click
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh type $'\e[<0;99;7M'; ... $'\e[<0;99;7m'   -> 03-after-issue-click
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh keys C-c; ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh keys Enter   # quit for real
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh start 200 50; ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh keys 4   -> 04-reopened-after-quit
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh inner-type %0 'printf "superseded by td-9f8e7d\n"'
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh inner-keys %0 Enter
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh type $'\e[<0;100;10M'; ... $'\e[<0;100;10m'    -> 05-second-td-retargets
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh stop

What each capture shows
-----------------------
01-terminal-full-width
  The starting state: one shell filling the whole preview, its output holding
  both links — "wrote clicked.md:1" and "follow-up is td-1a2b3c". No pane tree
  yet; the preview is the single terminal leaf.

02-after-file-click
  After clicking the cell at row 6, column 92 — inside "clicked.md". The
  terminal now holds the left column and the document the right one, split
  along columns. The document's header reads "clicked.md   Raw   ×" and its body
  is the fixture file. This is the split that already worked before this work.

03-after-issue-click
  After clicking the cell at row 7, column 99 — inside "td-1a2b3c". This is the
  steel thread. Measured on this capture's own cells:
    - the vertical pane divider stands at column 140 on every content row,
      4 through 48: the terminal's column is uninterrupted top to bottom;
    - the horizontal divider is on row 26 and runs columns 142 through 198 —
      inside the right column only. Column 140 on row 26 is still the vertical
      divider, which is what "terminal at full height on the left" means as a
      grid rather than as a tree shape;
    - the document occupies the right column above that divider (header on
      row 4), the issue below it (header on row 27, "td-1a2b3c: Issue td-1a2b3c",
      then [open] task P2 and the stub's body).

04-reopened-after-quit
  The same three panes after Ctrl-C, Enter on the quit confirmation (a real
  process exit) and a fresh start into the workspaces plugin. The layout, the
  document and the issue all come back; the issue was re-fetched rather than
  restored from a cached body, which is why its text is the stub's current
  answer. 06-persisted-layout.json is the state this reopen read: the terminal
  beside a rows-split of doc and issue, with the issue leaf carrying its td id
  and the document leaf its path.

05-second-td-retargets
  After emitting "superseded by td-9f8e7d" in the same shell and clicking it.
  The tree is unchanged — still three panes — and the existing issue leaf now
  shows td-9f8e7d. This is the agreed default: a second issue click retargets
  the issue leaf, mirroring how a second file click retargets the document pane.

06-persisted-layout.json
  The paneLayout the quit left in the private state tree, copied verbatim.

What this proves, and what it does not
--------------------------------------
Proven visually, in a running binary: the three-leaf placement and its geometry,
the issue leaf's rendering, the quit/reopen round trip, and the retarget default.

Not proven here: the divider-drag recapture, which needs a drag gesture rather
than a click and is measured in Go instead
(TestDividerReleaseRecapturesTheTerminalWithoutActivation in
internal/plugins/workspace/doc_panes_test.go, with the transport half in
internal/tty/resize_debounce_test.go). The refusal path — a box too short for
the stacked split — is also Go-only
(TestAnIssuePaneThatWillNotFitLeavesTheLayoutAlone), since at 200x50 every split
fits.

The placement rule these captures exercise is a default, not a settled design:
planPaneOpen is one pure function, asked by every kind of click, and M1 of
docs/plans/active/workspace-windowing-system.md replaces it outright rather than
unpicking it from the click paths.
